q: Under Ind AS 109, a financial asset is measured at amortised cost only if:
o: The hold to collect model applies and the cash flows are SPPI
The instrument is a debt security quoted in an active public market
Management designates it as amortised cost at initial recognition
The instrument has a fixed maturity of more than one financial year
why: Both the hold to collect business model and the SPPI test must be met for amortised cost. Quotation in an active market and maturity length are irrelevant to classification, and there is no free designation into amortised cost.

q: A loan contains a term allowing the borrower to prepay at an amount that includes reasonable compensation for early termination. This term:
o: Automatically fails the SPPI test, forcing measurement at FVTPL alone
Requires the prepayment feature to be bifurcated as a derivative
Requires the loan to be classified and measured at FVOCI instead
Does not by itself fail SPPI, as reasonable compensation is allowed
why: Ind AS 109 accepts prepayment features where the amount substantially represents unpaid principal, interest and reasonable early termination compensation. Embedded derivatives are not bifurcated from financial asset hosts in any case, which is a key change from the old standard.

q: An equity investment not held for trading is designated at fair value through other comprehensive income. On disposal:
o: The cumulative gain held in OCI is reclassified to profit or loss
Only the dividends received are recognised in profit on disposal
The cumulative gain stays in equity and is never recycled to profit
The entity restates the prior period comparative figures on disposal
why: For the equity FVOCI election there is no recycling of amounts to profit or loss on disposal, which distinguishes it from the debt FVOCI category. Dividends on such equity investments are recognised in profit or loss when the right to receive is established.

q: A portfolio of debt instruments is managed with the objective of both collecting contractual cash flows and selling, and the cash flows are SPPI. The correct classification is:
o: Amortised cost, with interest under the effective interest method
FVOCI, with cumulative gains recycled to profit on derecognition
FVTPL, with all fair value movements taken to profit or loss
Equity FVOCI, with no recycling of gains on disposal at all
why: The hold to collect and sell business model with SPPI cash flows produces debt FVOCI, where amounts accumulated in OCI are recycled on derecognition. Interest, impairment and foreign exchange for such assets still go through profit or loss.

q: Under the general expected credit loss model, an instrument moves from Stage 1 to Stage 2 when:
o: Credit risk has increased significantly since initial recognition
The borrower has defaulted on the contractual payments now due
The instrument has been outstanding for more than twelve months
The exposure exceeds the internal single borrower limit that is set
why: Stage 2 is triggered by a significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition, at which point lifetime ECL is measured but interest is still computed on gross carrying amount. Actual credit impairment moves the asset to Stage 3, where interest is computed on the net carrying amount.

q: For a Stage 3 credit impaired financial asset, interest revenue is calculated by applying the effective interest rate to:
o: The gross carrying amount before deducting any loss allowance held
The original contractual amount of the loan that was advanced
The amortised cost, being gross carrying amount net of allowance
The fair value of the collateral held as security for the loan
why: Once an asset is credit impaired, interest is recognised on the net amortised cost after deducting the allowance. Applying the rate to the gross amount is correct only for Stage 1 and Stage 2 assets.

q: The simplified approach under Ind AS 109 for trade receivables without a significant financing component requires:
o: Twelve month expected credit losses to be held at all times instead
Fair value measurement of the receivable at each reporting date
Losses only where objective evidence of impairment is present
Lifetime expected credit losses from the outset, with no staging
why: The simplified approach mandates lifetime ECL from day one and removes the need to track significant increases in credit risk. Recognising losses only on objective evidence is the superseded incurred loss approach.

q: Ind AS 109 requires that the rebuttable presumption of a significant increase in credit risk arises when contractual payments are more than:
o: More than 15 days past due on the contractual payments
More than 30 days past due on the contractual payments
More than 60 days past due on the contractual payments
More than 90 days past due on the contractual payments
why: The rebuttable presumption for a significant increase in credit risk is 30 days past due, whereas 90 days past due is the rebuttable presumption for default. Confusing the two thresholds causes assets to be staged incorrectly.

q: An expected credit loss measurement under Ind AS 109 must:
o: Reflect the single most likely outcome of the credit exposure
Be unbiased, probability weighted, discounted and forward looking
Ignore forward looking information so as to avoid any speculation
Use only the historical loss rates of the last three financial years
why: ECL is a probability weighted, discounted estimate that incorporates reasonable and supportable forward looking information available without undue cost or effort. Using a single best case outcome or purely historical rates fails the measurement objective.

q: An entity transfers receivables to a bank but retains a guarantee for the first 20 percent of credit losses and continues to collect from customers. Most likely the entity:
o: Neither transfers nor retains all risks, so the control test applies
Derecognises the receivables in full, since legal title has passed
Recognises a gain on sale equal to the full carrying amount involved
Reclassifies the transferred receivables to FVTPL at the date of sale
why: Where risks and rewards are neither substantially transferred nor retained, the control test applies and retained servicing plus a first loss guarantee typically means continuing involvement. Legal transfer of title alone does not achieve derecognition under Ind AS 109.

q: Reclassification of financial assets under Ind AS 109 is permitted:
o: Whenever management changes its intention for a single instrument
Only with the prior approval of those charged with governance given
At each reporting date, for any of the measurement categories used
Only on a business model change, applied prospectively and rarely
why: Reclassification is driven solely by a change in business model, is expected to be very infrequent, and is applied prospectively. Equity instruments and assets designated at FVTPL under the fair value option can never be reclassified.

q: For a cash flow hedge, the effective portion of the gain or loss on the hedging instrument is:
o: Recognised in profit or loss immediately as it arises each period
Adjusted against the carrying amount of the hedged item in all cases
Recognised in OCI and accumulated in the cash flow hedge reserve
Deferred and presented as a contract asset on the balance sheet
why: The effective portion goes to OCI in the cash flow hedge reserve, with any ineffective portion recognised immediately in profit or loss. Adjusting the hedged item carrying amount is the fair value hedge mechanic, not the cash flow hedge mechanic.

q: Under Ind AS 109, hedge accounting requires an economic relationship between hedged item and hedging instrument, the effect of credit risk not dominating value changes, and:
o: A hedge ratio matching the quantity actually used to hedge the risk
A quantitative effectiveness result within the 80 to 125 percent band
Retrospective effectiveness testing carried out at each reporting date
Formal approval of the hedge relationship by the audit committee
why: Ind AS 109 replaced the bright line 80 to 125 percent test with a principles based hedge ratio requirement linked to actual risk management. Retrospective bright line testing is no longer a condition for hedge accounting.

q: A financial liability is measured at FVTPL and the entity elects to present changes attributable to its own credit risk in OCI. Those amounts:
o: They are recycled to profit or loss when the liability is settled early
They are added to the carrying amount of the liability every period
They must be reversed if the credit spread of the entity narrows
They are never transferred to profit, though they may move in equity
why: Own credit risk gains and losses presented in OCI are never recycled to profit or loss, avoiding the counterintuitive result of booking profit as credit quality deteriorates. Transfers within equity are permitted.

q: Which cost treatment is correct at initial recognition under Ind AS 109?
o: Transaction costs are added to the fair value of the FVTPL assets
FVTPL costs go to profit at once, other categories adjust cost
Transaction costs are always capitalised whatever the category
Transaction costs are recognised in other comprehensive income
why: For FVTPL instruments transaction costs are expensed immediately, while for amortised cost and FVOCI they are included in the initial measurement and amortised through the effective interest rate. Treating them uniformly misstates both the carrying value and interest income.

q: A trade receivable is sold at a deep discount to a factor without recourse, and the entity has no continuing involvement. The correct treatment is:
o: Retain the receivable on the balance sheet and recognise a liability
Reclassify the receivable to FVOCI at the date of the factoring
Derecognise it and take the difference on consideration to profit
Recognise the discount as a reduction of revenue under Ind AS 115
why: Where substantially all risks and rewards have transferred with no continuing involvement, the asset is derecognised and the loss on sale hits profit or loss. The discount is a financing cost of the factoring arrangement, not an adjustment to the original transaction price.

q: When auditing an ECL model, which element is ordinarily the HIGHEST estimation uncertainty?
o: The macroeconomic scenarios, their weights and probability of default
The gross carrying amount of the loan book extracted from the ledger
The contractual rate of interest charged on each of the individual loans
The number of loan accounts making up the portfolio at year end
why: Macro scenario selection, scenario weighting and PD estimation involve significant management judgement and drive the loss allowance materially. Ledger balances, contractual rates and account counts are objectively verifiable data with low estimation uncertainty.

q: A debt instrument classified at FVOCI is impaired. The loss allowance is:
o: Deducted from the carrying amount of the asset on the balance sheet
Recognised only at the point of derecognition of the debt instrument
Ignored, because the fair value already reflects the credit risk
Charged to profit or loss with the offsetting entry made in OCI
why: For debt FVOCI the asset stays at fair value on the balance sheet, so the ECL charge goes to profit or loss with the offset in OCI rather than reducing the carrying amount. Assuming fair value alone handles credit risk would leave the impairment charge missing from profit or loss.
